title: The NGC and its modern counterpart
caption: The galaxies NGC 4424 and LEDA 213994, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: LEDA 213994, NGC 4424 · constellation Virgo · about 30 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image shows two galaxies plainly. The larger is NGC 4424, and just below it sits a smaller, flatter, bright galaxy called LEDA 213994. Their names tell a story of their own.

A few cosmic objects have charming nicknames, like the Sombrero Galaxy or the Horsehead Nebula, but most are known only by catalogue entries. NGC 4424 comes from the New General Catalogue of Nebulae and Clusters of Stars, compiled in 1888. It has 7840 entries, mostly larger, brighter objects that early stargazers could spot more easily.

LEDA 213994 comes from the far more modern Lyon-Meudon Extragalactic Database, created in 1983 at the Lyon Observatory and containing millions of objects. Many NGC objects keep their older names simply because they were catalogued first. As for the acronym, LEDA may appeal partly because Leda was a princess in Ancient Greek mythology.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.70 x 2.67 arcminutes) and distance (30 million light years), the frame spans roughly 24,000 × 23,000 light-years. Its light set out about 30 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, using visible, near-infrared and very broad filters. The packet does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Part of the data is near-infrared light, invisible to the eye, and both galaxies are far too faint to see without a telescope.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Because the NGC ranks among the biggest catalogues in astronomy, many of Hubble's Pictures of the Week feature NGC objects. NGC 4424 lies about 30 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo.
alt: A larger galaxy with a smaller, flatter bright galaxy just below it.
